card.name: Tsamiko
card.era: Klephtic/armatoloi tradition; iconic of the Greek War of Independence (1821-1830)
card.tagline: Mainland 3/4 men's line dance of the klephts.
card.profile: A popular mainland Greek folk dance in 3/4 meter, also called Kleftikos for its association with the klephts who fought in the War of Independence. Slow, strict tempo emphasizing 'attitude, style and grace' over steps; dancers link hands bent 90 degrees at the elbows in a line/open circle. The lead dancer performs high acrobatic leaps (scissor-like kicks) supported by the second dancer. Danced almost exclusively by men, sometimes in the fustanella; most popular in Central Greece (Roumeli), the Peloponnese, Thessaly and Epirus. Played by zournas and daouli, or clarinet, violin and laouto (English Wikipedia; Domna Samiou Association).
card.insight: The name means 'dance of the Chams' (from Tsamouria/Chameria), though musicologist Samuel Baud-Bovy noted the Greek tsamiko was not actually danced among Cham Albanians; it is performed at national commemorations of the 1821 revolution.
